PullRequest.Title: agent Host: List legacy Copilot CLI sessions in  agent Host when migration is enabled
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- List all adoptable legacy Copilot CLI sessions, rather than only archived sessions, when migration is enabled.
- Make unopened legacy sessions accessible in the Agents window while preserving adoption on open and existing editor deduplication.
- Keep behavior unchanged when migration is disabled.
- Add regression coverage for repeated discovery, adoption, refresh, restart, reconnect, and legacy-provider removal.

## Validation
- 408 focused tests passed.
- End-to-end local and WSL-hosted migration tested in the Agents window and chat editor using isolated profiles.
- Verified preserved history, archived sessions, existing/recreated worktrees, expected missing-branch errors, and zero duplicate fixture entries after refresh, reload, and host restart.

To test manually, enable `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli`, restart the relevant Agent Host, and verify legacy sessions appear once and retain their history when opened.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added await, provider-supplied chat value, metadata stripping, database implementation, batch size, limiter, and globally serialized transaction path are all explicit in code. Exact milliseconds vary with profile size and storage speed, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SQLite transactions and catalog header/chat SELECTs on the agent-host database
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added work is O(N) database transactions for N newly discovered adoptable sessions (up to 250 per discovery batch, with further batches for larger histories); database serialization prevents the four-way discovery limiter from coalescing or parallelizing these reads.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased migration/discovery latency and serialized database I/O on the session-surfacing critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, announcements did not perform this default-chat catalog read; active adoptable sessions were rejected before announcement work, and archived announcements did not request a default chat.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every first announcement of an adoptable legacy session now awaits `_readDefaultChat`, which falls through to `readCatalogSnapshot([session])` when no summary has yet recorded the chat.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `const defaultChat = readSessionEhcliAdoptable(meta._meta) ? await this._readDefaultChat(meta.session) : undefined;` introduces the awaited per-session catalog lookup directly on the surfacing path.
Findings.Title: Reuse the discovered chat instead of rereading every catalog
Findings.Impact: On a profile with a large legacy Copilot CLI history, enabling migration delays discovery registration and delays later sessions becoming addressable in the Agents window while the host executes one extra SQLite transaction per newly surfaced session.
Findings.Evidence: Copilot discovery already constructs `IAgentDiscoveredChat.chat` with `deriveLegacyDefaultChat(session)`, but `_toSessionMetadata` explicitly removes `chat` before `_registerDiscoveredChats` calls `_announceSurfacedSession`. With no live/evicted/announced record yet, `_readDefaultChat` invokes `IAgentHostDatabase.readCatalogSnapshot` for one session. That database method runs a transaction with header and chat SELECTs through the single `_transactionSequencer`. Discovery publishes batches of up to 250 candidates; AgentService processes four concurrently, but these added catalog reads serialize at the database boundary.
Findings.Recommendation: Carry the already-known `IAgentDiscoveredChat.chat` through registration/announcement (or prefetch default chats for the batch) and pass it to `_surfacedSessionSummary`, avoiding a one-session catalog transaction per announcement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Migration-enabled discovery and surfacing of unopened legacy Copilot CLI sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Copilot SDK catalog enumeration and marker classification publish batches; AgentService registers/synchronizes each candidate and must finish `_announceSurfacedSession` before that candidate is announced. The newly added default-chat read is awaited on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK catalog call per discovery scan, returning the full SDK session catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK enumeration was already performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before candidates can be classified and emitted

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each candidate's extension-host CLI marker and resolve its legacy working directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per candidate, limited to 4 concurrently and processed in batches of 250
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same marker and directory reads already classified adoptable sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish for a candidate before it is published

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per newly registered candidate, limited to 4 at the service layer
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Active adoptable sessions were already registered and synchronized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one session's catalog snapshot to resolve its default chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra transaction per first announcement; up to 250 serialized transactions per emitted batch and more across larger histories
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No default-chat read occurred during announcement; active adoptable sessions returned before announcement work and archived announcements did not request the chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited immediately before announcing the row, delaying candidate availability and batch registration completion

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All newly discovered adoptable sessions not already known to Agent Host. Copilot scans the full SDK catalog and emits batches of up to 250; there is no age cutoff for adoptable legacy sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider classification is limited to 4, AgentService registration is limited to 4, but `readCatalogSnapshot` is serialized by the agent-host database transaction sequencer, so the added default-chat reads have effective database concurrency 1.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider deduplicates unchanged discovery signatures and `_announcedSurfacedKeys` prevents repeat reads after a successful announcement in the same host lifetime. A cold first announcement has no recorded state-manager default chat and reads SQLite; warm already-announced sessions avoid it. The provider already has the chat URI, but that value is stripped before announcement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the supplied chat is stripped, the added await falls through to a globally sequenced two-SELECT transaction before first announcement, and multiplicity follows the discovery batch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of legacy sessions and SQLite latency vary by user and storage, but profiles can retain hundreds of SDK sessions and the code explicitly supports 250-item discovery batches.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out; carry the known chat or batch-prefetch defaults.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Sessions and Sessions window display deduplication during refresh, reconnect, and adoption
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each consumer merges cached/provider rows, converts the collection to an array, and synchronously filters duplicate legacy/twin resources before rendering or returning sessions; no filesystem, database, network, subprocess, or IPC operation is performed inside the changed helper.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of merged session rows, including both legacy and local agent-host twins; effective cardinality is the complete displayed collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-threaded collection scans; no concurrency or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The full underlying maps retain both rows for lookup and cache identity. Deduplication is recomputed on getter calls and has no memoized result; it allocates bounded sets proportional to matching rows. Cold and warm behavior are the same.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the helper is O(N) and boundary-free; insufficient evidence of user-visible regression from the extra linear pass.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session getter frequency depends on UI observation/render behavior, but the diff preserves linear complexity and adds only one linear scan/set for collections that contain legacy rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the changed dedupe remains linear and does not establish a concrete rendering or latency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read-state actions for an unopened legacy session's default chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A client action enters the per-session passive metadata sequencer. When a surfaced summary exists, the adoptable marker is checked in memory and the action returns before persistence or restore. Only the fallback with no summary queries registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up and decode the sessions_v2 row when no surfaced summary exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lookup per read-toggle action lacking a surfaced summary
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old path proceeded toward restore/rejection rather than performing this adoptable lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before deciding to drop the action in the fallback path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of read-toggle actions delivered for unopened legacy chats; normally one action per user/client state change, serialized per session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session sequencing; independent session keys can run concurrently, with no new global burst shown by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Surfaced summaries are the warm in-memory path. If absent, `_isRegisteredAdoptableSession` performs a single database lookup; there is no added retained cache. The new summary now normally contains the default chat, so the in-memory path applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the branch and lookup, low that realistic action volume creates a regression; the branch also avoids substantially heavier restore work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The summary-missing fallback should be uncommon because this PR announces listed legacy sessions; event frequency is not demonstrated as high.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the fallback query is bounded and the changed mechanism prevents a full session restore, so no independent performance regression is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and adopting a listed legacy session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench resolves the legacy resource to its agent-host twin, then Agent Host reads the catalog, asks the provider to adopt, registers if necessary, and restores session state before the editor can use it. The diff supplies default-chat metadata earlier but does not add work to the open/adoption restore itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected session catalog and persist registration/catalog state
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same adoption path ran when a legacy row was opened.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call the Copilot provider's adoption operation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for the selected eligible session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening a legacy session already probed adoption.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the host claims and restores the session

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/move legacy session metadata and session storage during adoption/restore
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing adoption performed the same storage work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected session per open action; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restore/adoption uses existing per-session sequencing and catalog synchronization; separate opens may use separate keys.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An announced summary makes the default chat available in memory before open. Adoption clears the adoptable marker; existing editor/session deduplication prevents duplicate rows. Cold adoption performs existing catalog/provider/storage work; subsequent resident opens reuse state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the expensive adoption boundaries are pre-existing and per-open.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage and provider latency vary, but no changed line increases open-time boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes discoverability and summary metadata, not the expensive open/adoption work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced legacy discovery, agent-host listing/announcement, workbench deduplication, read-toggle handling, and adoption. Reported one per-session serialized catalog-read fan-out introduced on the discovery surfacing path; no other changed mechanism met the performance evidence threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
